overview: Time Interconnect Technology is a Hong Kong-headquartered, Luxshare Precision Industry-controlled manufacturer of customised interconnect products with over 30 years in the cable/connector industry, operating manufacturing facilities across Shanghai, Jiangsu, Jiangxi and Guangdong (PRC), Japan, Thailand, Vietnam and Mexico. It supplies copper and optical-fibre cable assemblies, digital cable products, copper wire, medical device cables and servers on a contract-manufacturing (CMS/JDM-ODM) basis across telecommunication, data centre, medical equipment, industrial equipment, automotive and server end markets. Revenue has grown explosively (HK$3.6bn FY2022 to HK$12.4bn FY2025, and HK$10.1bn in H1 FY2026 alone) on the back of AI-driven data-centre and server demand plus the December 2025 acquisition of copper-wire maker DJC Group and the July 2025/July 2026 buildout of European cable maker Leoni Kabel via the Time Singapore joint venture.

business_model.summary: Contract manufacturer that produces custom cable assemblies, digital cables, copper wire and servers to customer specification (made-to-order, CMS basis), selling mainly to PRC and international OEMs/brand customers in a B2B2B model. The server/data-centre segment (JDM/ODM, deeply customised for brand customers) has become the dominant growth engine, while a newly acquired copper-wire sub-business (DJC Group) supplies both internal cable production and external customers including the controlling shareholder's group (Luxshare). Copper price pass-through is contractual (selling price auto-adjusts with copper price), so gross profit amount, though not margin, is largely insulated from copper price swings.
business_model.customer_type: B2B/B2B2B — PRC and international OEM brand customers across telecom, data centre, medical, automotive and industrial sectors; order-driven/project-based rather than recurring/subscription revenue
business_model.geographic_mix: Manufacturing in China (Shanghai, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Guangdong), Japan, Thailand, Vietnam and Mexico; reporting currency HKD with revenue/costs also in USD, RMB, Thai Baht, Vietnamese Dong, Mexican Peso and Euro (post Leoni Kabel, exposure extended to Germany, Poland, Hungary, Slovakia, Turkey and the Americas)

main_competitors: Leoni AG (now majority-owned by Time Interconnect via Time Singapore)
competitive_position.market_position: Mid-sized, fast-growing interconnect/cable-assembly and server JDM/ODM supplier riding the AI/data-centre capex cycle; not a top-tier global connector player by scale, but a key subcontracted manufacturing arm within the much larger Luxshare ecosystem (Luxshare itself is a major Apple supplier and one of the largest global EMS/connector groups)

moat_factors.description: Controlling shareholder Luxshare Precision Industry supplies technology know-how, customer relationships, subcontracting capacity and a growing Master Supply Agreement (annual caps raised from HK$240m to HK$3,497m for 2026 and HK$5,837m by 2028), giving Time Interconnect privileged access to Luxshare's customer base and production platform

Long operating history and engineering relationships support a 'preferred supplier' positioning with market-leading customers, but the business remains a contract manufacturer with limited pricing power of its own
December 2025 acquisition of DJC Group brings in-house copper wire supply across China/Thailand/Vietnam, reducing single-country sourcing risk and improving control over a key raw material

Facilities across China, Japan, Thailand, Vietnam and Mexico allow tariff-driven order migration (e.g., Linkz Mexico ramp benefiting from US tariff avoidance); Leoni Kabel adds Europe/Americas production
Selling prices automatically reset with copper price moves, protecting absolute gross profit (though not margin percentage) from commodity swings

weaknesses: Heavy dependence on controlling shareholder Luxshare both as a commercial partner (growing related-party sales caps) and strategic decision-maker, raising governance and arm's-length-pricing questions

Server segment, now the largest revenue contributor, carries structurally lower gross margins, compressing group-level profitability as its mix share rises (gross margin fell from 14.7% restated FY2024 to 11.8% FY2025)
Contract-manufacturing model with limited own-brand IP; revenue is order/project based rather than recurring, exposing the business to customer capex cycles
Multiple large, fast-executed acquisitions (DJC Group, Leoni Kabel/Time Singapore, several medical-tech startups) raise integration and capital-allocation execution risk
Heavy and increasing reliance on the AI/data-centre capex supercycle for incremental growth, which is a narrower, more cyclical driver than the diversified legacy cable business

growth_drivers: AI-driven data-centre and server demand: server revenue +132.1% in FY2025 and +68.3% in H1 FY2026; data-centre cable assembly +49.4% FY2025 and +22.8% H1 FY2026, with double-density MPO and multi-core fibre panels reaching mass production and lifting ASPs/margins

December 2025 acquisition of DJC Group (copper wire manufacturer, China/Thailand/Vietnam) adding vertical integration and a new ~29% of group revenue in H1 FY2026, with manufacturing bases that can serve US-bound sales outside China

July 2025 acquisition (by 49%-owned JV Time Singapore) and July 2026 full buyout of Leoni Kabel, a century-old German/European cable brand with facilities in Germany, Poland, Hungary, Slovakia, Turkey, Mexico and the PRC, extending the Group's global footprint and automotive/data-centre reach

Luxshare Precision Industry's strategic sponsorship: rising Master Supply Agreement caps (to HK$3,497m in 2026, HK$5,837m by 2028) and explicit management commentary that Luxshare is conducting a 'strategic review' to help the Group become an 'all-rounded network solutions and infrastructure provider', aligned with China's 'East Data West Computing' policy

Medical equipment diversification: continued investment in medical/health start-ups (UK wearable robotics, UK NHS digital workforce platform) and creation of the Medical Engineering and Innovation Council (MEIC) under the Federation of Hong Kong Industries, aiming to build a third growth pillar alongside cable/server and copper wire

Large capital raises (HK$1.63bn placing Feb 2026, HK$2.88bn placing May 2026) funding further M&A, overseas expansion and balance-sheet strengthening; inclusion in the HKEX Tech 100 Index from June 2026 broadening the investor base

business.risk: Customer and related-party concentration via Luxshare
business.description: A large and rapidly growing share of revenue flows through or to the Luxshare group (related-party sales caps raised from HK$240m to HK$3,497m for 2026 alone); third-party estimates put related-party revenue at roughly 45% of turnover. This creates dependence on a single controlling counterparty's commercial decisions and on Luxshare's own end-customer relationships (including Apple), with limited independent disclosure of arm's-length pricing terms

business.risk: Margin dilution from server-sector mix shift
business.description: The fast-growing but lower-margin server segment now accounts for the largest share of revenue, pulling group gross margin down from 14.7% (restated FY2024) to 11.8% (FY2025) and 12.6% (H1 FY2026) even as absolute profit grows

Multiple sizable, recently completed acquisitions (DJC Group, Leoni Kabel/Time Singapore, several medical-tech minority stakes) need to be integrated and must deliver the promised synergies; DJC Group contributed only one month of FY2025 revenue so its full-year run-rate and margin profile are largely unproven in the historical record

US tariff escalation since February 2025 has already reduced networking-cable segment revenue (-18.4% FY2025) and slowed medical-equipment export orders; further escalation could affect other segments despite Mexico/Vietnam/Thailand production diversification

financial.description: Receipts/payments span USD, HKD, RMB, Thai Baht, Vietnamese Dong, Mexican Peso and (post-Leoni) Euro; RMB appreciation added HK$193.7m to H1 FY2026 revenue, showing meaningful translation sensitivity

financial.risk: Rising debt from the DJC Group acquisition
financial.description: Bank loans rose from HK$243.2m (restated, FY2024) to HK$1,263.0m (FY2025), a 419% increase, driven by the DJC Group acquisition, alongside continued related-party borrowing from the Luxshare Group (HK$46.4m interest expense in FY2025) for working capital

Three placings since February 2026 (108m shares at HK$15.22, 138m shares at HK$21.00, raising a combined ~HK$4.5bn-plus net proceeds) have materially increased share count; while funding growth, this dilutes existing holders and signals heavy reliance on equity capital markets to fund M&A

regulatory.description: Extensive and growing connected transactions with the Luxshare Group (equipment purchases, subcontracting, leases, master supply agreements, Leoni Kabel buyout) require ongoing Hong Kong Listing Rules compliance and independent shareholder/director oversight of related-party pricing

Operations spanning China, Southeast Asia, Mexico and now Europe expose the Group to evolving export control, tariff and geopolitical fragmentation risk, particularly given its position inside a PRC-controlled corporate group supplying global technology customers

macro.description: A large share of recent growth is tied to the global AI/data-centre investment supercycle; a slowdown in hyperscaler or server-OEM capex would disproportionately affect the Group's fastest-growing, now-largest segment

Average copper price rose 8.7% in FY2025 and 38.7% in H1 FY2026; although pass-through protects absolute gross profit, large swings affect margin percentage, working capital (inventory/receivables) and reported revenue growth optics

Management repeatedly cites heightened geopolitical tensions, protectionist trade measures, and in H1 FY2026 a Middle East-driven energy price shock, as headwinds to global growth and corporate investment sentiment

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global interconnect/cable-assembly and server-component demand is being reshaped by the AI/data-centre investment boom (IMF projecting global growth easing from 3.2% in 2025 to 3.1% in 2026, but AI capex seen as a key offsetting growth engine); cloud adoption, big data, IoT and video streaming continue to support structural data-centre cable/server demand
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high — contract manufacturing/CMS revenue is order-driven and tied to customer capex cycles (notably AI/data-centre and consumer electronics), with copper and networking-cable legacy segments more exposed to macro/trade-policy cyclicality
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — the Group carries bank loans (HK$1,263.0m at FY2025) and related-party loans from Luxshare Group used for working capital, with finance costs of HK$59.7m in FY2025 and HK$64.3m in H1 FY2026; large recent equity placings have reduced reliance on debt funding
key_input_costs: Labour (headcount grew from 6,031 to 7,835 in FY2025, with total employee benefit expense up to HK$970.9m)

recent_developments.event: Completed acquisition of Dejinchang Investment Limited (DJC Group), a copper wire manufacturer with facilities in China, Thailand and Vietnam, contributing one month of FY2025 revenue (HK$354.5m) and continuing to supply copper wire to the Luxshare Group
Completed a HK$15.22/share placing of 108,000,000 new shares, raising net proceeds of approximately HK$1,634.5 million for strategic investments/acquisitions, overseas expansion and working capital
Board appointed two new executive directors (Chaung Kwai Wing, Hung Wai Lai William) and an independent non-executive director (Dr. Wu Che Yuen Justin)
Published FY2025 annual report: revenue HK$12,409.6m (+68.0%), net profit HK$783.6m (+69.0%), final dividend HK2.4 cents/share (2024: HK1.3 cents); FY2024 comparatives shown as 'restated'
Completed investment in a UK-based membership body operating a Digital NHS workforce platform (3,500 GP practices, 7,500 clinicians), extending the medical/health investment strategy

Completed a second placing of 138,096,000 new shares at HK$21.00/share, raising net proceeds (combined with February placing) of approximately HK$4,519.0 million in total; stock fell over 8% on the announcement
Included in the HKEX Tech 100 Index, which the company says should raise visibility with institutional and passive-index investors

Completed acquisition of the remaining 51% of Time Interconnect Singapore Pte. Ltd. (and thus Leoni Kabel GmbH) from Luxshare Precision Limited for an initial HK$12.7m (cap up to HK$40m / reported elsewhere as ~HK$460m total consideration including shares), making Time Singapore/Leoni Kabel wholly owned

Published H1 FY2026 interim results: revenue HK$10,066.1m (+107.4% YoY), profit for the period HK$827.8m (+163.9% YoY), gross margin 12.6% (down from 13.2%), driven by DJC Group consolidation and continued server/data-centre growth

recent_developments.date: 2026-11 (per Nov 2025 sourcing, effective into current year)
recent_developments.event: Luxshare Group Master Supply Agreement annual caps raised materially — 2026 cap increased from an initial HK$1,598m to HK$3,497m, with 2028 cap of HK$5,837m — reflecting expected further growth in related-party server/copper-wire sales volumes

items.target: No explicit numeric full-year guidance disclosed; management guidance language points to continued strong growth from server/data-centre and copper wire (DJC Group) segments
items.vs_prior: not applicable — no formal point guidance given
items.notes: Management commentary (H1 FY2026) notes record Q2 order levels in data centre and server businesses and continued capacity expansion in the PRC and Vietnam

items.metric: Related-party sales cap (Luxshare Master Supply Agreement)
items.target: HK$3,497m for 2026, rising to HK$5,837m by 2028
items.notes: Cap increased twice within roughly a year (from an original HK$240m, to HK$1,598m, to HK$3,497m for 2026) reflecting expected growth in related-party sales volume; this is a connected-transaction ceiling, not a revenue forecast

items.target: ~50% strategic investments/acquisitions, ~30% global business development/overseas expansion, ~20% working capital and balance-sheet strengthening (varies slightly by placing)
items.notes: Combined ~HK$4.5bn of net placing proceeds from Feb and May 2026 earmarked mainly for further M&A and overseas expansion, with some allocated to bank debt repayment

guidance.management_commentary: Chairperson Wang Laichun (also a senior Luxshare executive) and CEO Simon Cua emphasize that, 'supported by Luxshare Precision Industry's platform and strategic alignment,' the Group will continue pursuing organic and inorganic growth globally, aiming to become an 'all-rounded network solutions and infrastructure provider.' Management flags continued AI-driven structural demand for data centre and server products as the primary growth engine, with medical equipment as a secondary strategic focus, while cautioning that global growth is expected to ease in 2026 with risks tilted to the downside (tariffs, geopolitical tension, commodity volatility).

bull_case: Direct beneficiary of the AI/data-centre capex supercycle, with server and data-centre segments compounding at triple-digit and high-double-digit rates and now forming the majority of revenue

Strategic backing from controlling shareholder Luxshare Precision Industry — a top-tier global EMS/connector group and major Apple supplier — provides privileged access to technology, customers and subcontracting capacity, evidenced by sharply rising Master Supply Agreement caps

Rapid, well-funded vertical and geographic expansion (DJC Group copper wire, Leoni Kabel's century-old European cable brand and global footprint, medical-tech investments) diversifies revenue beyond the legacy cable-assembly business

Strong balance sheet post-placings: ~HK$4.5bn of fresh equity capital in 2026 funds further M&A and overseas expansion without materially increasing leverage, and HKEX Tech 100 Index inclusion should broaden the institutional shareholder base

Profitability has scaled faster than revenue in percentage terms in several recent periods (H1 FY2026 net margin 8.2% vs 6.5% a year earlier), showing operating leverage even as segment mix shifts toward lower-margin server sales
bear_case: Heavy and growing dependence on the Luxshare relationship for both commercial volume and strategic direction creates related-party concentration risk, with limited independent visibility into whether pricing and allocation decisions are fully arm's-length

Gross margin has been structurally declining (14.7% to 11.8% FY2025, pressured further by copper wire trading-like economics) as the business mix shifts toward lower-margin server and copper-wire revenue, meaning rapid top-line growth may not translate proportionally into profit growth

Aggressive, serial M&A (DJC Group, Leoni Kabel, multiple medical-tech minority stakes) funded substantially by dilutive equity placings raises execution and capital-allocation risk, and track record on integration/synergy realization is still unproven

Business is a contract manufacturer without strong independent brand or IP moat, exposing it to customer concentration, order volatility, and the risk that AI/data-centre capex growth decelerates or normalizes after the current supercycle

Exposure to US tariff escalation, trade-policy unpredictability and multi-currency translation risk (RMB, USD, Thai Baht, Vietnamese Dong, Mexican Peso, Euro) adds macro volatility to reported results
